sentences.text:
Heard Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Manoj Pandey, learned counsel for
informant, Sri Sunil Kumar Srivastava, learned A.G.A. and perused the records.

2.  The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.326 of 2022, (Special Sessions Trial No.940 of 2022), under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station-Amroha Dehat, District-Amroha after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 15.12.2022 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act) 1st, Amroha.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act) 1st, Amroha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. In the present case, father of the victim initially lodged an F.I.R. against the present applicant on 15.9.2022 making allegation that in the night of 13.9.2022 he has enticed her daughter aged about Kailash vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113530454/
1 19 years and kidnapped her from his lawful guardianship.

entities.text: Kailash vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that victim was traced on 18.9.2022 and thereafter she recorded under statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. wherein she declared herself to be in consensual relationship with applicant and has not stated anything adverse against him.
5. Learned counsel further submitted that victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. for the first time declared her age about 16 years and stated against the applicant and three other co-accused that they not only kidnapped her, but she was kept by them for seven days and was repeatedly raped.
6. Learned counsel further submitted that victim herself declared to be a major girl, however, on the basis of her educational documents, her age was determined about 16 years and seven months and also submitted that after investigation, charge-sheet has been filed only against the applicant and allegation made by the victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. against three other accused persons were found false.
7.

Learned counsel lastly submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 16.10.2022, there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
8.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail application and submitted that at this stage statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is found to be true qua to the allegation against the applicant that he not only kidnapped her, but committed offence of rape for about seven days.

Age of the victim was determined on the basis of her educational document i.e. less than 18 years,
therefore, her consent, if any, is immaterial.
9. Learned counsel for informant submitted that accused side has put pressure to settle issue.
However, when it was refused, a false F.I.R. was lodged by them wherein the victim and her family members were made accused, however, outcome of investigation is not on record.

10.Learned counsel for informant and learned A.G.A. have also failed to contradict that though victim has also named three other co-accused who have committed above referred offence, but nothing adverse was found against them during investigation.
11.LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is not need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

entities.text: Kailash vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text:
In the present case, on the basis of educational documents of victim, she is less than 17 years old,
therefore, she is a minor girl in terms of the provisions of Section 2 (d) of POCSO Act and Section 375-Sixthly of I.P.C., therefore, consent of a minor, if any, is immaterial.
13. From the facts referred above and submissions, it transpires that victim has not stated anything adverse in her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C., against the applicant.

However, she has made specific allegation against the applicant of kidnapping and rape in her statement recorded under Sections 164 Cr.P.C. along with three other co-accused, but the same was found false qua to other three accused persons, therefore, it appears to a case where the victim is trying to exaggerate the offence.
14. The Court is concious about the fact that victim is a minor girl, therefore, her consent, if any, is immaterial.

However, considering the facts of the present case, where the victim has tried to involve other persons also which was found false during investigation, therefore, the submission of learned counsel for applicant that it may be a case where the victim went with the applicant on her own will,
therefore, the applicant who is in jail since 16.10.2022, has made out a case for bail.

15. However, in order to remove any apprehension that applicant may influence the victim, it is directed that applicant shall not enter within the boundaries of Amroha for a period of three months from today except for the purpose of this case or with prior permission of Trial Court.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Trial Court will take all endeavour to record the statement of the victim.

17. Let the applicant-Kailash, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.

(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of the applicant, if there is no other legal impediment.

(v) Applicant has to appear on each and every date before learned Trial Court and any application for exemption of his appearance on vague ground could be a ground for cancellation of bail by learned Trial Court without even issuing notice.

18. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
19. The bail application is allowed.
20. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
